title: Require measured stage timings in readings of speed-up requests
summary: Add a rule to the reader's guidance: for any request to speed up the pipeline or landing, the reading cites the measured stage order and durations from job records (own checks, verification, CI) and estimates the expected gain from them before writing criteria. The audience is the reader agent and the user judging its readings. The rule goes in reader.md, kept inside the 2,000-token reader budget.

defaults_applied.how: Add a test that the reader prompt contains the rule and stays within budget; cargo test and clippy pass.
Criteria check the rule's text is in the compiled reader prompt and the budget test passes.
The rule itself requires cited or estimate-labelled numbers.
One focused prompt change with a test and a changelog entry.
Rule and decision entry are written plainly for outside readers.
A test enforces the rule's presence in the prompt.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The 'reading role's guidance' is crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md, which is compiled into the reader brief.
reader.md is near its 2,000-token budget (decisions.md notes it must not grow much), so the new line is short and may need trimming of wording elsewhere in the file.

Records are absent from the reader's copy, so the rule must say to cite durations from whatever job records the brief or repository docs provide, and to label the figures as an estimate if none are available.
A speed-up request is one about making the pipeline, checks, verification, CI or landing faster.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md states that for any request to make the pipeline or landing faster, the reading cites the measured stage order and durations from the job records (own checks, verification, CI) and estimates the expected gain from those numbers before writing acceptance criteria.
The new rule says to label any duration or gain not measured as an estimate, consistent with the evidence default, and does not remove existing rules.

Run `cargo test -p athena-context`: the reader budget check passes (reader set stays within 2,000 tokens) and a new test asserting the reader prompt contains the speed-up rule (stage order, durations, expected gain) passes.
Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.
CHANGELOG.md records the change, and docs/decisions.md has an entry giving the rationale and alternatives (such as putting the rule in a schema field description).

out_of_scope: Changing any pipeline or landing speed itself
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, or workflows
Changes to the producer or verifier prompts
